title: Business Travelers Just Want Some Time Alone
paragraphs: Business trips often include meetings, dinners and other events with colleagues and clients. But according to a new survey, many business travelers would prefer to spend their free time alone.
The survey was carried out online by Talker Research for the hotel company Hyatt between May and June 2026. It asked 2,000 American business travelers about their experiences on work trips.

The results showed that nine in 10 business travelers feel that their hotel room is the only place where they are truly "off the clock" during a work trip. In addition, 47% said they had gone back to their room instead of meeting other people for work. Some people even made excuses to get time alone. For example, 36% said they had pretended to have meetings to get some free time, and 33% said they had claimed to have other plans to avoid work dinners.
However, many travelers feel bad about this. In the survey, 46% said they felt guilty when they said no to optional work activities so they could relax in their room.
Business travelers also work a lot during trips. More than half, 53%, said they work most nights after their workday has ended, and 22% work every night.

Because of this, hotels are very important to business travelers. In the survey, 87% said their hotel can make or break a trip, and 79% said that staying in a good hotel helps them work better. The most important things in a hotel room were a comfortable bed and fast, free Wi-Fi.
Another study by the hotel company Hilton found similar results. It found that 27% of business travelers look for time alone on work trips to rest and get their energy back.
Jason Ballard of Hyatt said that, for frequent business travelers, a good hotel stay "is not necessarily about extravagance."
